overview:
Linda Sánchez, the Democratic incumbent, is favored to hold this Southern California seat against Republican Mitch Clemmons. The district leans Democratic by about nine points, and the broader 2026 environment also favors Democrats, pushing the expected margin well above twenty points. Sánchez has raised about $1.6 million and holds a large cash advantage, while Clemmons has raised under $6,000 and shows no outside support. Prediction markets on Kalshi and Polymarket price her win probability at 94 to 97 percent.

No public general-election polls are available for this race, so the forecast rests on district fundamentals, incumbency, and the lopsided money gap. That combination points to a comfortable double-digit Democratic win, with uncertainty wide enough to reflect the absence of direct polling.
